findings.evidence: Mathlib/Topology/UniformSpace/UniformConvergence.lean defines `UniformCauchySeqOn` and names its API `uniformCauchySeqOn_…`; Mathlib/Topology/MetricSpace/Cauchy.lean:70 uses `Metric.uniformCauchySeqOn_iff`. The declarations at lines 361–364 and 416–419 quantify both large indices and all `t ∈ Icc 0 T`, exactly expressing uniform Cauchy convergence on that set.
findings.fix: Rename both using `uniformCauchySeqOn` (and preferably state their conclusions via `UniformCauchySeqOn`), retaining `_of_mem` for the domain variant.
findings.issue: Both `exp_yosidaApproximation_cauchyOn_compact_of_mem` (line 358) and `exp_yosidaApproximation_cauchyOn_compact` (line 413) assert uniform Cauchy convergence on `Icc 0 T`, but `cauchyOn` obscures Mathlib’s standard predicate terminology.

summary: The compact-time results use a misleading nonstandard Cauchy name for uniform Cauchy convergence on a set.
